finding: The F-AHL29 fallback preserves correctness above cache capacity but repeated uncached rebuilds are expensive.
A fixed first-32/no-eviction policy retains about half the requests as hits in the strict 64-key round-robin workload.
In the grouped workload, keys 33-64 are rebuilt for every request; bounded replacement could exploit that locality.
A generic 32-slot LRU is not justified by this characterization because a strict 64-key round-robin working set would be vulnerable to full thrashing.
next_question: What bounded cache capacity/replacement policy minimizes rebuild work across realistic MultiSWAP locality patterns without making memory usage unbounded or degrading adversarial round-robin behavior?
nonclaims: No MultiSWAP application speedup is claimed from this synthetic cache benchmark.
